articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The GST Council, which meets Thursday, will seek to slash the refund period to around 17 days, which will include a maximum 10 days for
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The GST Council, which meets Thursday, will seek to slash the refund period to around 17 days, which will include a maximum 10 days for acknowledgement, beyond which it will be deemed to have been acknowledged, and seven days for processing. Currently, acknowledgement itself can take 21-45 days and the idea is to process refunds faster, officials said Tuesday. Currently, around 90% of the refunds are processed quickly.Similarly, the idea is to prune the time taken for registering for a GST number through a more automated process. While 61% of the registrations take place within three days, the plan is to automate processes so that the time taken for the remaining 39% of the applications is reduced from several days. But, officials also said that not all registrations take a long time as those for businesses below Rs 2.5 lakh turnover are given within 34 minutes on an average.For small businesses that operate in more than one state, the GST Council will consider steps that will enable them to avoid the registration exercise across states if an e-commerce platform through which they sell has a recognised warehouse as a place of business. "Overall, nine out of 10 sellers on platforms will gain," an official said.In case of an entity looking to cancel its registration, the Centre and the states will discuss a proposal to do away with the physical verification of the premises by an official, where the presence of the businessman is required. If taxes are paid and returns are filed, registration will be cancelled, an official said, adding that the idea is to move to a trust-based system.Similarly, through a host of changes in the rules, govt is also keen to allow input tax credit on insurance, use of vehicles and other services. "ITC should be allowed in case of supplies, such as supply of passenger motor vehicle, leasing, repair, renting of motor vehicles, health and life insurance, outdoor catering, construction of telecommunication tower and pipelines, free samples and expired goods - as all are used in the furtherance of business," said Sameer Gupta, who leads the EY India tax practice.This will come along with changes that will allow businesses to claim credit for taxes paid during the entire process even if some entities in the chain have not complied. "Invoice matching system now links what a seller reports with what a buyer claims, and mapping of input and output ledgers with the summary return completes the link. This is a major shift in how GSTN system works. Fake credit can be identified close to where it arises and stopped before it travels down the chain. articles.title: E-way bills point to fertiliser diversion
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The humble e-way bill, introduced to check truck movement nine years ago, has helped govt track diversion of fertiliser.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The humble e-way bill, introduced to check truck movement nine years ago, has helped govt track diversion of fertiliser. Thanks to the electronic tool, which is to be used by every truck carrying goods valued at over Rs 50,000, just a preliminary check at the height of the fertiliser crisis post Iran war showed that trucks meant to deliver goods at designated locations were making detours or were making one trip too many."The ministry did some preliminary checks when, after the war started, there were concerns that there may be some fertiliser shortage and there were also fears of hoarding and diversion," an official said.The finance ministry, which undertook the analysis, then alerted the fertiliser department. Diversion of fertiliser, which is highly subsidised, is not a new phenomenon but govt is more than keen to crack down on it in the wake of the renewed pressure on prices, although supply has eased and govt has stocked up. The fertiliser ministry also maintains Integrated Fertiliser Management System (iFMS) to track the movement of subsidised fertiliser.A parliamentary standing committee recently noted that there was leakage during transportation. "Partial unloading and re-routing during transit from rake points to remote districts (particularly in hilly terrain - J&K, Uttarakhand); movement without valid documents (Madhya Pradesh: 28 cases of unauthorised movement in 2025-26); delayed or non-reporting of receipt at destination (were observed)," it said in a report tabled in Aug.The parliamentary panel recently said that neem-coated urea was seeing diversion to industrial units such as plywood and resin factories, diesel exhaust fluid (DEF) units and for cattle feed manufacturing, especially in Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka, and Punjab.According to agriculture ministry data, in 2025, 4.8 lakh raids were conducted across the country and over 17,000 notices were issued, while nearly 7,000 licences were cancelled with 850-odd FIRs registered against defaulters.In fact, there have been multiple studies by agencies which also point to smuggling of fertiliser from India to neighbouring countries through trucks.You use AI every day. articles.title: FMCG Q2: Margins under pressure
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) companies are grappling with heightened commodity cost inflation amid a sharp rebound in crude oil prices while
articles.body: MUMBAI: Fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) companies are grappling with heightened commodity cost inflation amid a sharp rebound in crude oil prices while the impact of weak monsoons is slowly showing up in pockets of consumption, companies said in their Q2 updates even as they estimated strong revenue and volume growth for the quarter.The broader takeaway is that demand continues to hold up but margins are under pressure. Analysts and brokerages attributed much of the growth to a mix of GST cut benefits, low base and selective price hikes, projecting a weak outlook for the sector going ahead.The markets are mirroring the underlying pressure-FMCG Nifty Index is down nearly 16% since Jan 1. "With sustained cost headwinds, we may see growth moderation ahead, which alongside margin strain could stress FY27 earnings," analysts at HDFC Securities said in a note. Godrej Consumer Products (GCPL) flagged intensifying input cost pressures during the quarter and said that uneven monsoon conditions also weighed on consumption. "We are responding through a combination of calibrated pricing actions, cost-saving initiatives, supply chain efficiencies," GCPL said, estimating high-teens revenue growth and high single-digit underlying volume growth.Dabur, which expects consolidated revenues to record double-digit growth, said that operating margins were impacted by inflationary pressures, partly offset by price increases."While volume trends have been stable so far (led by GST benefit and soft base), margin trajectory may not improve as expected with RM (raw material) pressures not abating. Hence, despite low double-digit sales growth, earnings growth is unlikely to be exciting or surprise positively for most of the names," analysts at JM Financial said.The impact on volume growth will be visible from the March quarter, said independent consumer consultant Akshay D'souza. "The story in FMCG is that profitability is under pressure," D'souza said. Even as companies have refrained from passing on the full impact of commodity inflation to consumers so far, selective hikes have negated much of the benefits from reduced prices post GST cuts. Further price increases in the coming months cannot be ruled out."Domestic demand remained resilient during the quarter, even as the operating environment stayed volatile through the period. Looking ahead, we remain optimistic on consumption trends, while closely monitoring the evolving inflationary conditions," said Marico.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Indian economy is expected to grow 7.1% in 2026-27, against 6.6% estimated earlier, on the back of strong domestic demand and exports,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Indian economy is expected to grow 7.1% in 2026-27, against 6.6% estimated earlier, on the back of strong domestic demand and exports, despite global headwinds, the World Bank said Tuesday.The multilateral agency is the latest to revise its projections after India's growth accelerated to 7.8% during the first quarter of the current financial year, prompting upgrades from ADB, S&P, Moody's and other global entities, which typically take a cue from official data. In 2027-28, the World Bank expects the Indian economy to grow by 7.2%."Medium term prospects are strong, but external risks are elevated, including downside risks related to global oil prices, El Nino and stock market corrections that would result in capital flow volatility," World Bank said in a statement.It expects the "strong" momentum in industry and services to continue, with the reforms that have been undertaken - consolidation of labour codes, GST reforms, tariff rationalisation , IBC amendments, and investments in physical and digital infrastructure. In the medium-term, growth is projected to average 7.1% between 2027-28 and 2028-29, with a narrowing current deficit and declining inflation."Strength in the rest of the economy is expected to make up for agricultural weakness," the World Bank said, adding that the sub-par monsoons will likely reduce agricultural output and rural demand, while increasing food inflation. This will add to existing pressure from higher energy prices.Besides, the biannual update said India is well positioned to harness AI, thanks to its large technical workforce, globally integrated IT sector, and digital public infrastructure. Currently, it is ranked 10th in AI readiness, behind the US (rank 1), China (2nd) and South Korea (6th).According to a survey by the global financial institution, 23.4% of Indian firms use some form of AI, compared with 42.7% of firms in the US. articles.title: Volatility triggered by CAS surges on NSE on expiry day
articles.summary: MUMBAI: After a break of about two weeks, Closing Auction Session (CAS) again played truant during Tuesday's late session as weekly derivatives contracts
articles.body: MUMBAI: After a break of about two weeks, Closing Auction Session (CAS) again played truant during Tuesday's late session as weekly derivatives contracts on NSE were expiring. Within a span of just 30 seconds-between 15:20:00 and 15:20:30-Nifty rallied a little over 300 points or about 1.5%, and in the next eight minutes fell about 240 points or 1.1%.Sensex also saw a sudden spike but a relatively smaller one during CAS. The index rose about 350 points or 0.5% and then fell from the high. To address issues of CAS-related volatility, markets regulator Sebi is working on changing some rules for the session.At the close of Tuesday's trading, sensex was up 685 points or 1% while Nifty closed 220 points or 1% up at 22,776 points. The gains in the indices, which marked the second consecutive day of rise, came on the back of falling Brent prices that went below the psychologically important $100/barrel level, along with strong global cues.According to Vinod Nair, head of research, at Geojit Investments, crude oil prices slipped below the $100-mark after a large G7 stockpile release and alternative supply measures helped offset disruptions to vessel movements through the Strait of Hormuz."Coupled with strong Q2 business updates from financials and retail along with supportive global cues, the decline in oil prices improved investors' sentiment and supported a rebound from the oversold levels. Domestically, attention now shifts to the Q2 earnings season for silver lining amid weak sequential expectations due to elevated input costs," Nair wrote in a note to investors.Market players said Dalal Street investors would remain cautious ahead of the RBI policy decision on Wednesday, "with the focus firmly on the central bank's inflation outlook and guidance on further policy tightening," Nair said.Interestingly, the day's gains in the two indices came despite Rs 2,961 crore worth of net selling by foreign funds in the stock market, BSE data showed. articles.title: 4G mobiles make a comeback on costlier 5G smartphones
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Costlier smartphones are slowing India's shift to 5G.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Costlier smartphones are slowing India's shift to 5G. Rising component costs are driving a comeback for 4G devices as buyers seek better specifications at affordable prices.Shipments of 4G smartphones are expected to grow 3% in 2026 even as the overall market declines, according to Counterpoint Research. Their share of smartphone shipments is projected to rise from 11% in 2025 to 13% this year and 15% in 2027.The shift is particularly visible in the Rs 10,000-20,000 segment, where the number of smartphone makers offering 4G models has increased from two in 2025 to 12 this year. "India's 4G recovery is increasingly extending beyond the traditional entry-level segment," Counterpoint senior analyst Prachir Singh said. Buyers in this price band are seeking better device experiences without the higher price associated with 5G, he added.India's overall smartphone shipments fell 11% year-on-year in the June quarter, Counterpoint said, with record-high memory costs triggering multiple price hikes and weakening demand, particularly at the lower end."Building a 5G phone under Rs 15,000 that doesn't compromise on the overall experience has become extremely challenging," Sumit Singh, SVP and head of products at Lava International, told TOI. "At the same time, consumer purchasing power hasn't grown to match these rising costs."Lava continues to prioritise 5G but has revisited its strategy for the sub-Rs 15,000 market. Demand, Singh said, is "not for the cheapest phone" but for better value, specifications and ownership experience. Brands like Xiaomi, Infinix, Realme have also launched 4G phones this year.Counterpoint research director Tarun Pathak said the shift could outlast a temporary response to higher prices because component costs are unlikely to normalise quickly. For manufacturers, this creates room to offer better-equipped 4G devices at affordable prices, while buyers increasingly weigh connectivity against the overall experience. articles.title: Cabinet OKs 10,000 crore SME growth fund
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Union Cabinet on Tuesday approved the setting up of Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund (SGF), aimed at catalysing growth-oriented capital for
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Union Cabinet on Tuesday approved the setting up of Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund (SGF), aimed at catalysing growth-oriented capital for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to enable the emergence of champion enterprises across manufacturing, services, technology, innovation-driven sectors and strategic value chains. The fund was announced in the last budget, focusing on providing equity, liquidity and professional support for the MSME ecosystem."There are existing funds which provide equity support but majority of them focus on early-stage enterprises and cover majorly micro enterprises. A structural gap exists for equity growth capital for SMEs. The fund will consider SME's operating in industrial clusters in Tier II and Tier III cities," government said in a statement.
